title: Boundary wall cumulative length, R50 and above, frontage greater than 8.5 m (65%)
text: C3.4.4 Boundary walls may be built in accordance with Table 3.4c provided: i. boundary walls are located behind the street setback; ii. overshadowing does not exceed the limits of C3.9.1; and iii. they are finished to an equivalent standard to the rest of the development, to the satisfaction of the decision-maker. Table 3.4c Lot boundary setbacks, R50 and above where frontage is greater than 8.5m: maximum boundary wall height 7m; maximum boundary wall length 14m length, at which point the wall is to be set back a minimum of 3m measured from the lot boundary for a minimum length of 3m, with a cumulative maximum of 65% of the lot boundary the wall abuts.

exceptions.label: abuts an existing or simultaneously constructed wall of similar or greater dimension (C3.4.5)

replaces.note: two-thirds measured behind the setback -> 65% of the whole boundary

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: The 'cumulative' total of boundary wall along one boundary is taken as building.boundary_walls.max_pct_of_boundary (the fact vocabulary has no separate cumulative-per-boundary fact).

verified.note: Values clear on the page, but the page says 'cumulative maximum of 65%' while the encoded fact (building.boundary_walls.max_pct_of_boundary) is the longest single wall as % of its boundary; cumulative length of all walls on one boundary is not captured.
